sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Manchester City host Crystal Palace at Etihad Stadium with City chasing the top and Palace safely mid-table (City 2nd, 74 points; Palace 15th, 44). Sofascore’s model leans strongly towards the hosts (home win 68%, draw 20%, away win 12) and assigns a 43% chance that both teams score.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: City are unbeaten in 8 and in their last 5 have 4 wins and 1 draw, generating heavy shot and corner volumes. Palace’s last 5 read 2-1-2 and they have conceded in all 5, though they continue to create chances. Recent City home matches show sustained pressure and late goals.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: City won the most recent meeting 3-0 at Selhurst Park; the previous clash there finished 1-0 to Palace despite City dominance. Across recent matchups City hold the edge, and these games have often opened up after the break.

sections.subtitle: Season and tactical outlook
sections.text: City lead the league for possession (60.5%) and accurate passing (88.5%) and top big chances created (114). Their defence remains reliable (32 conceded, 15 clean sheets). Palace sit 15th (38 scored, 44 conceded) and tend to rely on quick breaks, with away games frequently featuring chances at both ends.

sections.subtitle: Players to watch
sections.text: Erling Haaland leads the league with 26 goals and is supported by in-form Jérémy Doku (4 goals, 2 assists across the last 5). For Palace, Jean Philippe Mateta (11) and Ismaïla Sarr (8) provide the main threat, while Adam Wharton has created 14 big chances. Note: Rodri is listed as absent, which may slightly affect City’s midfield control.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Stuart Attwell averages 3.5 yellows per match (red 0.14). City’s discipline is moderate (1.83 yellows per match) and this head-to-head has typically been low on cards. City lead the league in corners (6.29 per match) and their recent home games have produced high corner totals, though past head-to-heads have often been lower.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: City’s control of territory and chance creation, combined with Palace’s recent defensive record, supports the model’s strong home lean. Expect sustained City pressure and a higher share of corners for the hosts, with the chance of both teams scoring below even (43%).

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Manchester City lead Crystal Palace 2-0 at the interval at the Etihad Stadium. The hosts struck through Antoine Semenyo on 32 minutes and Omar Marmoush on 40 minutes, both finishing right-footed moves. City have controlled territory and possession and look in command of the contest.

halftimeSections.subtitle: First-half summary and key stats
halftimeSections.text: City dominance is clear: 75% possession, 3 shots on target, 6 corners, 21 penalty-area entries and 39 final-third entries. Expected goals: City 0.85, Palace 0.41. City also won 6 possessions in the final third and edged aerials (55%). Palace offered limited threat: 1 shot on target, 2 corners, 8 final-third entries and 5 box entries. Defensive workload for Palace was heavy, with Jaydee Canvot (6 clearances) and Maxence Lacroix (4) busy.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical notes
halftimeSections.text: City’s structure has been stable, with Joško Gvardiol stepping high on the left and midfield rotations freeing Phil Foden between the lines. Foden delivered 2 assists, 2 big chances created and 5 key passes, repeatedly finding runners. Bernardo Silva supported circulation and counter-pressing. City’s counter-press has pinned Palace back, reflected in 6 high regains. Palace have sat deep in a narrow block, looking to spring Jean Philippe Mateta and the wide outlets Brennan Johnson and Yéremy Pino on transitions. Will Hughes provided the most creative moments from midfield.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Palace began with a brief positive spell before City took control. From around the 6th minute, City enjoyed a long attacking phase with only short interruptions. After a short lull near the quarter-hour, City reasserted control, building sustained pressure that intensified around the half-hour, leading to the goals. The half ended with City pressing strongly again.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Player focus
halftimeSections.text: Phil Foden has been the main playmaker (2 assists, 5 key passes). Marmoush and Semenyo have been decisive with their finishing. Gvardiol’s forward involvement added an extra runner and one effort on target. For Palace, Tyrick Mitchell registered their only shot on target, while Hughes produced their best creative pass. Dean Henderson has faced steady pressure and required help from central defenders, with Canvot and Lacroix making multiple clearances.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Discipline and corners
halftimeSections.text: No cards were shown in the first half. Corners: City 6, Palace 2. Given the flow, expect City to add 3-5 more corners after the break, with Palace at 1-2. Discipline outlook: with Palace defending deep and City controlling the ball, 1-2 second-half bookings are likely, more so for Palace under sustained pressure.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: City are well placed to manage the game while continuing to create. Their press and territorial control should persist, and further chances look likely, especially if Palace open up. Palace need earlier support to Mateta and quicker progression to Johnson and Pino to threaten in transition. Without a change in field position, Palace’s attacks will remain sporadic.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: City to extend their lead and close the game out. Prediction: City score the next goal and win 3-0. Expect 1 goal after the break, with Phil Foden the most likely scorer from City’s current creators and runners.
